Chapter 8: The Power of Questioning—Rediscovering Curiosity.
Think about this: there’s a moment in every life when a single question shifts everything. Maybe it’s just “Why?” Or maybe it’s that bolder, “What if?” When you ask, the world cracks open—and suddenly, you see possibilities you might’ve missed before.
Picture a middle-aged accountant, stuck in the same routine day after day. One day, he wonders if there’s more to life than just numbers and spreadsheets. He starts asking questions—about his work, his relationships, his dreams. At first, the answers are tough to face. He realizes he’s been living on autopilot, following a script he never even wrote. But the more he keeps asking, the more he uncovers—new interests, fresh connections, even a sense of hope he’d forgotten was possible.
Here’s something to remember: curiosity is a real force. It’s what drives growth. It sparks creativity. It’s what keeps us from getting stuck. Most of us start out curious, but over time, we’re taught to stop questioning so much. In schools, it’s the right answer that gets you the gold star—not the best question. At work, efficiency matters more than exploring new ideas. And in families, kids are often told to follow the rules, not to wonder why they exist.
But you know what? The world needs more people who ask questions. We need folks willing to challenge the usual way of thinking, to imagine new possibilities, and to admit, “Hey, I don’t have all the answers,” but still keep searching anyway.
Let me give you another example. There’s a nurse who’s frustrated with the limits of her job. She starts to ask why certain policies exist. Turns out, a lot of them are based on old habits, not real evidence. By questioning how things are done, she helps her team discover better ways to care for patients.
See, the power of questioning isn’t just about finding better answers. It’s about taking back control—about not just settling for things the way they are. It’s about believing that change is possible, that things really can be different.
Most people never get back to that natural curiosity they had as kids. They settle for easy answers, stick to familiar routines, and cling to certainty. But for those who do dare to ask, the rewards are huge. They find real meaning, new purpose, and a sense of possibility you just can’t find anywhere else.
